comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations prescribe a 150 EC Mathematics major and a 30 EC minor. The example includes the Mathematics first-year project, the first two options in the two-course choice group, the first eligible 2026–2027 option in the second group and the first eligible additional elective.
components: The example uses the Mathematics project from the two first-year project choices.
Mathematics & Society: Ethical and Professional Aspects
Builds on second-year mathematics and the research, writing and presentation skills from the first-year project.
One of the two restricted options illustrated here. Builds on calculus, linear algebra and linear systems.
The second restricted option illustrated here. Builds on group theory and linear algebra.
A 2026–2027 example from the separate 5 EC restricted group. The course assumes basic linear algebra, modular arithmetic, algorithms and some Python.
Project Systems Theory is the example for the 5 EC elective. It builds on Linear Systems.
Complete year one and earn 150 EC in Mathematics, including project preparation. The study programme and career portfolio require approval.
The degree includes a 30 EC minor. Its courses depend on the minor chosen.

alternatives.label: Mathematical methods, algorithms & autonomous systems
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is weighted toward calculus, linear algebra, numerical mathematics, probability, algorithms, optimisation and autonomous computational systems. It does not claim the target’s proof-based pure-mathematics spine.
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, probability and numerical methods to model systems. Apply programming, algorithms and optimisation to problems in robotics, vision and decision-making under uncertainty.
progression: Programming and Mathematical Methods precede advanced computing and mathematics. Linear Algebra supports Robotics. Machine Learning precedes Neural Networks & Deep Learning.

alternatives.label: Probability, statistical modelling & computational research
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum emphasises probability, inference, multivariate statistics, econometrics, Monte Carlo simulation, machine learning, research design and meta-analysis, with mathematics and programming as foundations.
alternatives.concept: Use probability, statistical models and computation to answer empirical questions. Combine research design, econometrics and evidence synthesis with numerical methods, programming and machine learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with Alternative 1, this route replaces AI ethics, image processing, robotics, optimisation and reinforcement learning with research methods and statistics, empirical domain preparation, software development, econometrics and meta-analysis: five courses (37.5 EC) on each side are unique.
progression: Mathematical Methods precedes probability and numerical methods. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics. Brain and behaviour and applied statistics prepare for evidence synthesis and meta-analysis.

candidates.label: Probability, statistical modelling and computational research
Pure proof-based structures and advanced analysis

blocks: Both develop statistical modelling; UCR applies multivariate models in behavioural research rather than mathematical statistics.
Both develop programming for problem-solving; UCR teaches general Python rather than a mathematics-specific scientific-programming course.
Both use logic, sets and proof. Groningen extends this foundation into a sustained analysis and algebra sequence.
Both introduce differentiation and integration. UCR also uses complex numbers and differential equations in a dynamic modelling project.
Both directly study systems, vectors, matrices and linear spaces; Groningen continues to a second dedicated course.
Both establish probability distributions; UCR combines probability with statistical inference and simulation.
Both use interpolation, integration and equation-solving algorithms. UCR tests accuracy and stability with Mathematica, while Groningen uses Python.
Both use differential equations and feedback to study linear systems. UCR emphasises signal processing and transforms. Groningen includes controllability and state observation.
Both extend calculus; UCR includes multivariable and complex-valued functions but not the target analysis sequence.

selection.assessment: Two UCR options support mathematical and computational modelling or statistical inquiry. A further option in pure mathematics would require sustained proof-based analysis, topology, group theory, geometry and algebra beyond the available courses.

notes.text: The UCR options share work in mathematical methods, probability and computation. Groningen requires a sustained sequence in proof-based analysis, topology, algebra and geometry, along with a 15 EC Mathematics research project.

audience.programmeDescription: Mathematics at the University of Groningen develops mathematical proof, abstract reasoning, and analytical and computational methods. Students study algebra, analysis, geometry and probability before completing an independent Mathematics project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in mathematical computation and autonomous systems or in statistical modelling and research. Groningen gives more sustained attention to mathematical proof, analysis and abstract structures.
